Registration changes and related records



Table 32: H01 changes relative to the preregistered or otherwise expected analysis.






Topic
Preregistered or expected
Analysis used



Placement
Chest measurements were primary and near-eye measurements a robustness repeat.
Near-eye measurements are primary; chest measurements are complementary and placements are not pooled.


Inclusion and support
Protocol eligibility and fixed daily/hourly coverage exclusions defined the sample.
Verified participant-day coverage is followed by metric-specific support; every fitted model reports its exact rows and support hours.


Sleep and non-wear
Logged non-wear and sleep exclusions were applied without a fully specified state hierarchy.
Diary sleep has precedence, invalid non-wear is masked consistently, and sleep measurements are described as the bedside environment rather than ocular exposure.


Upper light boundary
Values above 120,000 lx were to be removed.
The verified analytical melEDI signal retains values strictly below 100,000 lx.


Darkest-window level
The level metric used the five darkest hours.
The approved metric is the mean melEDI during the darkest 10 hours.


Threshold timing
The timing outcome was the midpoint of the longest period above 250 lx.
The registered midpoint of the longest qualifying period is retained. Mean timing above 250 lx melEDI is a distinct circular duration-weighted metric and is labelled as an adapted sensitivity; period construction follows verified continuity and support rules.


Site and latitude
One model included both site and latitude.
Because each site has one latitude, fixed-site and linear-latitude models are fitted separately on identical rows and compared for adequacy.


Photoperiod scope
Photoperiod adjustment was specified for duration metrics.
Photoperiod is included in the common model implementation for all 17 metrics.


Response models
Linear mixed models were specified generically.
Each metric uses its approved Gaussian transformation or Tweedie log-link response model.


Multiplicity
False-discovery-rate control was required within H1 but the exact vectors were not specified.
Four separate complete 17-test Benjamini–Hochberg families are used for site, photoperiod, latitude, and site-versus-latitude adequacy.


Site follow-ups
Site coefficients were reported without a fixed hierarchical follow-up rule.
Only after a supported overall site test, each site is compared with the equally weighted overall site mean and the site contrasts are adjusted within metric.


Variation, uncertainty, and exact samples
Conditional R² and significance-dependent component summaries were used without joint interval estimation or exact model-specific sample reporting.
Marginal and conditional R², participant-associated share, and non-overlapping term part-R² summaries use 1,000 successful joint bootstrap refits and 95% intervals; exact model-specific samples are reported.


Model comparison
Fixed-effect structures had been compared using REML-derived criteria.
Gaussian fixed-effect comparisons use maximum likelihood; final Gaussian estimation uses REML where applicable.


Full-day construct
The intended relation between worn exposure and sleep-period environmental measurement was implicit.
The 24-hour record retains both constructs but keeps their interpretations distinct.


Melanopic daylight efficacy ratio
The submitted implementation averaged available momentary melEDI-to-photopic-illuminance ratios; the preregistration did not specify a ratio-of-integrals replacement.
MDER is the arithmetic mean of viable one-minute melEDI-to-photopic-illuminance ratios. Both channels must be finite and strictly positive, and at least 720 viable minutes are required on the complete 1,440-minute local wall-clock grid.


Interdaily stability and intradaily variability
Incomplete repeated-day support could enter the dynamics metrics.
Dynamics metrics use verified temporal support and report participant-level model rows plus contributing participant-days.


Windows, periods, and timing
Missing intervals could be bridged or incomplete windows summarized.
Windows and continuous periods use support, continuity, gap, wrapping, and tie rules fixed before modelling.


melEDI dose
Dose could be a partial sum without a defined support denominator.
Dose is time-sensitive and retained only with the approved interval support.


Time axes and source epochs
A single local time axis and one assumed source epoch were used.
Absolute time governs ordering and duration, local wall time governs clock metrics, repeated fall-back bins are handled explicitly, and each source epoch is respected.


Software environment
R 4.5 and earlier LightLogR/API versions were named.
The analysis uses the verified R 4.6.1 project library and pinned contemporary package APIs.


Participant-day plausibility
The preregistration and submitted implementation use coverage and signal-validity rules but do not specify exclusion of an otherwise eligible complete exact-zero melEDI day.
An otherwise eligible participant-day is excluded only when every finite one-minute melEDI value is exactly 0 lx; individual zeros remain valid and the former inclusion is retained as a fixed data sensitivity.


Pre-sleep duration
The label implied a single three-hour window before sleep.
The outcome is calendar-day cumulative time below 10 lx melEDI across every diary-defined pre-sleep interval; values strictly above six hours trigger an audit warning but are not capped.


Darkest-10-hour midpoint
The clock response was linearized around noon.
The primary conversion subtracts 24 hours only for values strictly after 16:00; the noon cut is a registered same-row sensitivity.



The central registration record classifies each entry as a current scientific deviation, a current qualification, resolved implementation history, or technical provenance.

title: H01 analysis preparation and provenance
text:
H01 asks whether personal light exposure differs among study sites. The analysis treats the near-eye sensor position as primary because it samples light closer to the eyes during wear, while recognizing that it does not directly measure retinal exposure. The chest sensor position provides complementary evidence about light measured at the chest, not ocular exposure. The 17-response package includes melanopic equivalent daylight illuminance (melEDI), an illuminance weighted for melanopsin-related sensitivity, and distinguishes an overall site association from photoperiod and absolute latitude.
The current MDER construct is the arithmetic mean of viable one-minute melEDI-to-illuminance ratios. Both channels must be finite and strictly positive, and at least 720 viable minute ratios are required for a retained participant-day MDER value.
This record explains which data and code produced those results, why each operation was needed, what it contributed, and what evidence shows that it behaved as intended. The sections follow the data-to-result sequence.
A model frame is the exact set of rows and variables used for one fitted model. Each response-specific frame is fixed before that model is fitted.
The H01 results report presents the scientific findings and its linked registration-record summary. Model estimates and 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs), model checks, influence results, and joint-refit summaries are read from stored outputs. This page does not fit or compare models, regenerate predictions, or repeat resampling.
False-discovery-rate (FDR) adjustment is applied separately to each of four complete 17-test families. A participant-day is one participant contributing one retained daily record on one local calendar day under the H01 day definition. Where a site-average estimate is reported, it is an average across sites that gives each site equal weight.

title: H01 analysis preparation and provenance
text:
8. Limitations and qualifications

The observational design does not identify causal effects of site, photoperiod, or latitude.
Site and latitude are structurally linked because each site has one latitude; separate same-frame models address estimability but do not remove geographic confounding.
Near-eye measurements are primary but are not direct retinal measurements; chest measurements are complementary and are not ocular exposure.
Model-check warnings require response-specific interpretation even when the optimization and inferential fit remain acceptable.
Measurement-support hours were not retained for the gap-timing-unaware dataset and therefore remain unavailable rather than reconstructed.
Term-specific part-R² summaries can overlap and must not be added.

NoteDarkest-10-hour mean data provenance



Eight primary darkest-10-hour mean records had numerical values indistinguishable from zero and are stored as exact zero. Each of the four affected primary darkest-10-hour mean branches retains at least 1,000 successful joint refits, with unchanged support, model-check, sensitivity, and claim disposition. The other 16 metric fits, the gap-timing-unaware darkest-10-hour mean fits, and the melanopic daylight efficacy ratio result set are unchanged by this bounded normalization.








NoteMDER production provenance



The MDER amendment replaced only the MDER branches with the approved mean of viable one-minute ratios and then recomputed the complete affected 17-test FDR vectors. Exactly eight MDER targets each retain 1,000 successful joint refits. Across 12,000 attempts, 11,998 succeeded and 8,000 were retained; two failed warning attempts were excluded. The focused verifier passed with no support change from the accepted MDER point gate, and the bounded integration preserved every non-MDER model and result artifact.


How to examine or reproduce H01
A reader can inspect the chain in four passes:

compare h01_contract.R with the two pinned analysis-dataset manifests to confirm the 17 responses, eight runs, transformations, and formulas;
compare the sample and retention displays above with model_rows.csv, sample_flow.csv, and H01_exact_samples_by_site.csv;
follow the producing script and SHA-256 identity in each manifest, using the stored model, bootstrap, diagnostic, table, and source-data files; and
read the H01 results report alongside its full-precision source tables rather than inferring numeric values from figure pixels.

Changes to shared metric preparation must be made upstream and propagated to every affected hypothesis. A display-only change can instead be made from the stored reporting objects without refitting the models or repeating the bootstrap.






TipReader takeaway



The H01 result comes from two verified analysis datasets, one declared model implementation for 17 responses, exact response-specific model frames, four complete multiplicity families, stored joint-refit bootstrap draws, and separate diagnostic and sensitivity records. This page connects those pieces without changing the scientific result.

Result

Convergence and coefficient rank
Converged; rank 2,333/2,333
Numerical fit completed at full coefficient rank.


Full-model in-sample R²
0.775 (95% CI 0.739 to 0.804)
Describes fit to these observations; it is not cross-validated performance.


AR(1) correction
ρ = 0.623; lag-1 0.623 → 0.083
Most average 30-minute residual dependence was removed.


Participant-day residual dependence
median lag-1 0.097; 95th percentile 0.458

Residual spread
RMSE 0.702; cor(|residual|, fitted) 0.202; max |residual| 5.69
Residual spread changes with fitted exposure and tails remain.


Basis-dimension checks
common k-index 0.999 (check p = 0.435); participant 0.999 (check p = 0.455)
No evidence that the available temporal basis was too small.


Sum-to-zero site constraint
verified; max |sum| = 2.57e-15
Site curves are identifiable deviations around the global time effect.


Nonlinear-term overlap (concurvity)
common/site = 0.999/0.992
The global and site bases overlap strongly; interpret complete curves and contrasts, not isolated coefficients.









The model converged at full rank, the basis-size checks did not indicate that the available time bases were too small, and the AR(1) correction reduced overall lag-1 residual correlation from 0.623 to 0.083. These are strengths for estimating average daily patterns.
The residual checks are not ideal. The QQ plot has an S-shaped departure from normality, and the line of observations at response -1 reflects the large number of exact zeros after the \log_{10}(\mathrm{melEDI}+0.1) transform. Residual magnitude also increases modestly with fitted exposure. Some participant-days retain positive lag-1 correlation. In addition, concurvity, the overlap among nonlinear terms, is high between the global and site time bases even though the sum-to-zero constraint is satisfied at full rank. The model is therefore adequate for a conditional description of mean curves and their complete contrasts, but it is not a perfect generative description of the full zero-heavy response distribution. Isolated smooth coefficients should not be interpreted as independent effects.

The chest model also converged at full rank. The AR(1) correction reduced overall lag-1 residual correlation from 0.607 to 0.070. Its basis-size checks were acceptable. The chest model is therefore corroborating evidence with the same interpretive limitations as the near-eye model.

H02 analysis preparation and provenance
text:
The scientific question was whether daily patterns of melanopic equivalent daylight illuminance (melEDI) differed among sites and whether differences among people within sites were larger than the differences among sites. The near-eye sensor position was primary because it measures light closer to the eye, but it is not a direct retinal measurement. The chest sensor position was analysed separately as complementary evidence and is not a measure of ocular exposure.
A participant-day is one participant’s observations on one local calendar date. Participant-day counts therefore describe repeated recorded days, not additional independent participants.
This page explains which data and code produced the reported H02 result, why each analytical step was needed, and what evidence shows that the processing and model behaved as intended. The companion H02 results report presents the scientific findings.






NoteHow to use this provenance page



This page explains the input and sample checks, model construction, model checks, and links between analysis code and accepted stored outputs. Rendering verifies file identities. A model frame is the exact set of rows and variables used for one fitted model. Rendering also calculates descriptive summaries from the H02 model frames. It does not fit a model, estimate an autocorrelation parameter, calculate model predictions, rerun a bootstrap, or recompute a Shapley allocation; those results are read from the listed output files. The result report lists the H02 preregistration deviations.

2. Fitted samples and model frames
Code and purpose
scripts/hypotheses/H02/build_h02_model_data.R sources two function modules:


h02_contract.R fixes the input identities, model specification, scenario registry, transform, and reproducible seeds;

h02_data.R validates keys, joins temporal provenance, creates the fitted support, defines residual-sequence starts, and constructs the all-available and placement-matched samples.

The script writes eight H02-only frames: two preparation rules × two placements × two sample definitions. The all-available near-eye frame is the primary sample. The all-available chest frame is complementary. The placement-matched frames retain only participant-day clock bins available for both placements and are sensitivity analyses, not a pooled model.
Within each frame, participant identifiers are prefixed by site, and participant-day identifiers combine site, participant, and local date. Rows are ordered using verified true elapsed time within those groups; local wall-clock time remains the coordinate used to describe the daily profile.

Why the response was transformed
The fitted response is \log_{10}(\mathrm{melEDI}+0.1\ \mathrm{lx}). The offset retains exact-zero observations and maps them to −1. The transformation compresses a range that extends from darkness to tens of thousands of lux, but it does not make the zero mass disappear. section: 3. Response transformation and nonlinear model construction
text:
3. Response transformation and nonlinear model construction
Exact selected formula
H02 used a nonlinear GAM analysis. A generalized additive model (GAM) allows the association with local clock time to bend across the day rather than forcing it to follow a straight line. The fitted response is log10(melEDI + 0.1 lx); a back-transformed curve applies the inverse transformation and returns to melEDI in lux.
scripts/hypotheses/H02/h02_modeling.R contains the fitting functions; h02_contract.R supplies their fixed specification. The exact Wilkinson formula was:
response ~
  s(time_hour, bs = "cc", k = 12) +
  s(time_hour, site, bs = "sz", k = 12) +
  s(time_hour, participant, bs = "fs", k = 10) +
  s(participant_day, bs = "re")
The first smooth is the global time effect, the site-average daily curve: it gives every site equal weight and joins smoothly at midnight. The sz term estimates site-specific departures that sum to zero, so no site is treated as the reference. The participant factor smooth represents remaining differences in daily shape among people after the time and site patterns are considered. The participant-day random effect represents remaining day-to-day level shifts within a participant after those patterns are considered; it moves an entire fitted day up or down.
Only the global time effect is forced to join at midnight in the primary model. A sensitivity analysis also makes the site and participant deviations cyclic.
Model settings

How the selected model was applied
The primary near-eye model is fitted first by run_h02_analysis.R. Reduced versions without the site pattern, participant pattern, or participant-day intercept are fitted with the same estimated AR parameter to compare model structures. The full structure is retained, and the identical selected structure is then applied to the other seven H02 frames. Each scenario estimates its own boundary-aware AR parameter from its preliminary residuals.
For every fitted scenario, the script writes the selected model, a checkpoint, site-curve predictions, fitted term contributions, residual summaries, and the stored 2,000-draw hierarchical variation bootstrap. The following fit table is read from model_fit_summary.csv; no fit is performed here.

6. Model checks and influence assessment
run_h02_temporal_diagnostics.R reads the stored selected models and model frames. It verifies coefficient rank and convergence, basis dimensions, sum-to-zero constraints, midnight continuity, boundary-aware residual behaviour, concurvity, and participant/site influence. Concurvity is overlap among nonlinear model terms that makes their separate contributions harder to distinguish. gratia is used for the formal concurvity wrapper; mgcv supplies the fitted GAM machinery and core model checks (diagnostics).
build_h02_reader_diagnostics.R converts the diagnostic source objects into the compact near-eye and chest model-check figures used in the H02 results report. Neither script changes the selected formula. Key accepted stored outputs are:

How to examine or reproduce H02
A reader can examine the analysis in four passes:

inspect h02_contract.R and input_hashes.csv to confirm the frozen input files and model specification;
compare the descriptive samples and support displays above with sample_counts.csv and the model-frame RDS files;
follow the producing script named in each output manifest, checking that its recorded inputs and outputs match the quantity being estimated; and
read the H02 results report alongside the result tables, model-check outputs, and source-data objects rather than attempting to infer results from a figure image alone.

Changes to source data or processing rules should be made before the hypothesis-specific model frames are built and then propagated to every affected analysis. Changing H02 alone would otherwise break comparability with the other hypotheses. Alternative H02 model choices should remain clearly labelled sensitivity analyses until their estimands and model checks are established.






TipReader takeaway



The H02 result was not generated inside a single opaque notebook. It came from a verified set of source files, H02-only model frames, a reusable temporal-model implementation, separately recorded inference and model checks, stored cluster-bootstrap evidence, and checksummed outputs. This page shows how those pieces connect without changing the reported scientific result.

title: H03: Self-reported light source and measured personal light exposure
text:
Principal results
The additive primary model and the category-by-site interaction model do not impose the same mean structure. The additive model forces every site to share one category ratio and estimates that common ratio from all participant-hours; its site-average indoor-electric estimate is 88.9 lx. The interaction model first estimates each site-category cell and then gives every site equal weight on the fitted log-mean scale; its corresponding estimate is 85.1 lx. The difference reflects the supported category-by-site interaction, not a different sample or outcome.
The preregistered additive-model omnibus remains the primary inferential test. Because that common-effect model is descriptively restrictive, all category means, ratios, 95% CIs, and site summaries from this point use the accepted category-by-site interaction model. The principal display is Figure 1, followed by the detailed values in Table 1.

These descriptive site-average estimates use the accepted category-by-site interaction model. Each site receives equal weight on the fitted log-mean scale before back-transformation to melEDI in lux. The 95% CIs account for related observations within participants using participant-clustered HC1 covariance. No p-value is attached to a different-model estimate; the additive primary omnibus is reported separately. The complementary chest external light during sleep category lacks one site-category cell, so its site-average estimate across all eight chest sites remains non-estimable.








For near-eye melEDI, the category-by-site interaction model gave a site-average outdoor-daylight mean of 959.6 lx (95% CI 786.8–1,170.2), or 11.274 times the indoor-electric mean (95% CI 8.709–14.595). Outdoor electric was instead 9.4 lx (95% CI 6.9–12.8), or 0.110 times the reference (95% CI 0.078–0.156). The latter differs markedly from the additive-model summary because the outdoor-electric contrast varies strongly by site and is sparse in several site-category cells.
The complementary chest interaction model gave the same broad ordering for the six categories with estimable site-average results. The external-light- during-sleep site-average estimate remains absent because one chest site-category cell was unavailable. These separate placement fits do not establish that the two sensor positions are interchangeable.
Result source data and figure source data retain the unrounded estimates and untransformed melEDI values.

The interaction model can be read as

\mu_{sc} = A \times R_c \times D_{sc},

where (A) is the site-average indoor-electric mean, (R_c) is the category ratio to indoor electric light, and (D_{sc}) is a site’s deviation from the site-average mean for that category. It used the accepted 17,935 participant-hours from 140 participants, a Tweedie distribution with a log link, and the primary working power fixed at 1.539919. The model contains neither a participant-day intercept nor a temporal correlation term. It was fitted only for variance description and does not replace the accepted population-mean analysis or estimate participant-specific light-source slopes.

Point estimates use Nakagawa’s model-based variance decomposition with a lognormal distribution-specific variance approximation; no bootstrap intervals were calculated. The decomposition uses the observed participant-hour frame rather than a site-average grid. The Shapley allocation refits hierarchy-valid nested models and averages both entry orders for site and light source; the interaction enters only after both main effects.








Marginal R² was 0.796 for the combined site, light-source, and interaction terms. Conditional R² was 0.876 after adding the participant intercept, a difference of 0.080. The adjusted ICC was 0.394 because it excludes fixed-effect variance from its denominator; the unadjusted ICC was 0.080 on the total model-based variance scale. A one-SD participant intercept was a 2.00-fold conditional expected mean relative to a participant at the model-average intercept while holding site and light source fixed. This is a common participant multiplier across categories, not a participant-specific category response. The variance decomposition is evaluated over observed participant-hours and is not a site-average estimand.
Marginal R² has no unique term decomposition. In the hierarchy-respecting Shapley analysis, the study-site component was 0.056 (7.1% of the full marginal R²), the light-source component was 0.710 (89.3%), and the site-by-light-source interaction component was 0.029 (3.7%). The three point allocations sum to the full marginal R². The analysis averages both hierarchy-valid entry orders for site and light source and introduces the interaction only after both main effects. It is consequently invariant to the chosen reference site and light-source category. It remains a descriptive allocation tied to this model-based R² definition and nested-model set, not a unique or causal partition of exposure variance.
The fit returned convergence code 0 without warnings, had a positive-definite Hessian, and was not singular. Its lag-one Pearson residual correlation was 0.288, so a participant intercept did not remove all within-participant temporal dependence. Exact zeros comprised 27.8%, compared with 39.8% under the fitted Tweedie distribution. The variance assessment is therefore descriptive, not evidence that the model predicts individual participant-hours well. Its Nakagawa R² values are not numerically interchangeable with the quasi-deviance R² and fixed-effect allocations in the preceding table. All five models used for the Shapley value function likewise converged without warnings, had positive-definite Hessians, and were non-singular.
Random-intercept assessment estimates and model diagnostics, together with the hierarchy-respecting Shapley allocation and nested-model checks, provide the complete stored point estimates and checks.

title: H03: Self-reported light source and measured personal light exposure
text:
Model checks
Both population-mean fits converged without warnings, retained full design rank, and had finite positive-definite participant-cluster covariances. Their working distribution nevertheless does not reproduce important features of individual-hour data.
Hours close together in time still show similar unexplained deviations: the technical lag-one residual correlations are 0.478 near eye and 0.615 at chest. Participant clustering protects coefficient uncertainty against arbitrary dependence within a participant, but it does not whiten residuals or turn the working Tweedie family into a calibrated probability model.
The discrepancy is clearest for zeros. Exact zeros comprise 27.8% of hours, whereas the working Tweedie relationship implies 85.2% near eye and 94.8% at chest. The model is therefore interpreted only as a log-mean model with participant-robust inference, not as an individual-hour prediction model or a model of zero probability.

text:
Exploratory nonlinear time-of-day context






NoteExploratory analysis



This nonlinear generalized additive model (GAM) analysis is separate from the preregistered category inference. The association with clock time is allowed to bend across the day rather than follow a straight line. The model uses one global cyclic time-of-day smooth plus sum-to-zero light-source and site deviations, participant curves, participant-day shifts, and a boundary-aware AR(1) correction. Light-source curves are ratios to the global daily smooth, not to indoor electric light, and no curve-wide test is made.


The exploratory model uses the untransformed one-hour geometric melEDI outcome with a fixed-power Tweedie mean and log link. This targets the conditional arithmetic mean rather than a back-transformed mean of a log-transformed outcome, which is why its daytime curves are substantially higher than curves for a geometric-scale centre. Site, participant, and participant-day smooths remain in the fitted model but are set to zero in the displayed global and category curves.
The temporal model is closer to the primary model’s raw-outcome mean target, but the two displays are not numerically interchangeable. The primary scalar averages over all contributed times and forms a site-average on its fitted log-mean scale. The temporal curves condition on clock time and show only the global and light-source components. Their values therefore need not average to the primary category estimates.

Exploratory linear latitude context
Latitude cannot be estimated alongside a saturated fixed-site term because each site has only one latitude. A separate exploratory model therefore replaces site with category-specific linear absolute-latitude slopes:
geo_medi_1h ~ 0 + light_source +
  light_source:absolute_latitude_10deg_centered
The coefficient for each category is the multiplicative change in expected one-hour melEDI per 10° farther from the equator. Preregistration deviations


Study-site structure (DEV-013). The registered random-effects architecture was not retained because site support did not justify the registered random-slope formulation and the participant-day component collapsed. The accepted analysis uses fixed study-site adjustment for the population-average category association and a separate category-by-site interaction model.

Response model (DEV-014). The registered Gaussian response formulation had inadequate distributional diagnostics. The accepted fixed-power quasi-Tweedie log-mean models with participant-clustered covariance accommodate the non-negative, right-skewed response and exact zeros. They are mean models, not calibrated zero-generating distributions.

Light-source categories (DEV-022). The analysis retains all seven prespecified categories under one placement-independent support rule and labels unsupported site-category cells rather than silently deleting categories.

Primary and site-interaction questions (DEV-023). The additive model supplies the primary six-restriction category omnibus; the separate category-by-site interaction model supplies descriptive means, ratios, and site-specific variation.

Multiple-testing adjustment (DEV-024). False-discovery-rate adjustment is applied to each explicitly assembled complete contrast family; category and site-interaction questions remain separate families.

title: H03 analysis preparation and provenance
text:
H03 asks whether all seven prespecified self-reported primary-light-source categories are associated with measured one-hour personal light exposure. The primary near-eye sensor position measures light close to the eyes. The complementary chest sensor position measures light at the chest and is not a measure of ocular exposure. The outcome is melanopic equivalent daylight illuminance (melEDI). The central estimand is the site-average geometric expected melEDI for each category and its ratio to indoor electric light. A site-average estimate gives each included site equal weight on the fitted log-mean scale; one back-transformation then returns the estimate to melEDI in lux.
This page identifies the data and code that produced the result, explains why each analytical operation was needed, and shows the recorded evidence used to check it. The analysis is observational and does not identify causal effects, health outcomes, or equivalence between measurement placements.
The H03 results report presents the scientific findings and its linked registration-record summary. The metric and model-ready input definitions are also documented in Preparation 04 and Preparation 06.






NoteScope of this analysis record



This page reads accepted estimates, 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs), omnibus tests, model checks, influence refits, sensitivity results, exploratory smooths, and latitude results from their recorded files. Its bounded display work does not fit or refit a model, calculate predictions, re-estimate residual autocorrelation, rerun a leave-one-site-out analysis, bootstrap, simulate data, or recalculate a variance allocation.

title: H03 analysis preparation and provenance
text:
1. Verified inputs
File identity
Six inputs determine the current analysis frames and displays: two accepted one-hour outcome files, the normalized diary, the predefined alternative preparation, the category dictionary, and the shared country-coded site registry. Their complete SHA-256 identities were recorded before estimation.

Show the R code used for this displayresult_input_ids <- c(
  "main_near_eye",
  "main_chest",
  "normalized_diary",
  "gap_timing_unaware",
  "category_dictionary",
  "site_registry"
)
input_labels <- c(
  main_near_eye = "Primary near-eye one-hour outcome",
  main_chest = "Complementary chest one-hour outcome",
  normalized_diary = "Normalized light-source diary",
  gap_timing_unaware = "Gap-timing-unaware one-hour outcomes",
  category_dictionary = "Light-source category dictionary",
  site_registry = "Shared country-coded site registry"
)

verified_inputs <- input_audit |>
  filter(.data$input_id %in% result_input_ids) |>
  mutate(
    current_sha256 = vapply(.data$path, artifact_sha256, character(1)),
    Input = unname(input_labels[.data$input_id]),
    Path = if_else(
      startsWith(.data$path, paste0(root, "/")),
      substring(.data$path, nchar(root) + 2L),
      basename(.data$path)
    ),
    `SHA-256 prefix` = substr(.data$current_sha256, 1L, 16L),
    verification_state = if_else(
      .data$current_sha256 == .data$sha256,
      "PASS",
      "FAIL"
    ),
    Verification = recode(
      .data$verification_state,
      PASS = "Verified",
      FAIL = "Review needed"
    )
  )
stopifnot(
  nrow(verified_inputs) == 6L,
  all(verified_inputs$verification_state == "PASS")
)

verified_inputs |>
  select("Input", "Path", "SHA-256 prefix", "Verification") |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::cols_width(
    Input ~ gt::pct(27),
    Path ~ gt::pct(51),
    `SHA-256 prefix` ~ gt::pct(15),
    Verification ~ gt::pct(7)
  ) |>
  gt::tab_source_note(
    "Complete 64-character identities are retained in artifacts/06_model_data/H03/H03_input_audit.csv."
  ) |>
  h03_gt(11)

Schema, keys, missingness, and category overlap
Outcome and diary records were joined one-to-one by site, participant, local date, and local clock hour. The primary model frames contain only admissible outcome hours with a non-missing primary-light-source category. Each retained record has one analysis category. The normalized diary also retains seven source-indicator flags: 7,109 near-eye hours and 8,012 chest hours had more than one true source flag, but the declared primary category was one of those true flags and remained the single mutually exclusive analysis label. Thus the overlap information was audited without duplicating an hour across categories.

    `Multiple source flags` = .data$source_flag_multiple,
    `Category-code conflicts` = .data$category_mapping_conflicts
  )
stopifnot(
  all(integrity_display$`Duplicate hour keys` == 0L),
  all(integrity_display$`Missing outcomes` == 0L),
  all(integrity_display$`Missing categories` == 0L),
  all(integrity_display$`Invalid outcomes` == 0L),

)

2. Model frames and support
Primary samples and repeated observations
A participant-hour is one accepted participant-by-local-hour record; a participant-day comprises one participant’s accepted hours on one local date. The primary near-eye frame contains 17,935 participant-hours from 140 participants, 801 participant-days, and nine sites. The complementary chest frame contains 19,512 participant-hours from 151 participants, 880 participant-days, and eight sites. Participant-hours repeat within participant-days and participants; therefore the nominal hour count is not treated as the number of independent units.

title: H03 analysis preparation and provenance
text:
3. Population-mean and category-by-site interaction models
Additive population-mean model
The prespecified primary question is tested with a population-mean GLM:
geo_medi_1h ~ site + light_source
geo_medi_1h is the one-hour zero-aware geometric melEDI in lux. The model uses a log link and a quasi-Tweedie variance function Var(Y | X) = phi * mu^1.539919. Site is a fixed factor with sum contrasts; light source is a fixed seven-level factor with indoor electric light as the treatment reference. The formula contains no random effect. Repeated participant-hours are addressed for inference with participant-clustered HC1 sandwich covariance, finite denominator degrees of freedom equal to the number of participant clusters minus one, and two-sided 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs). This interval calculation accounts for the fact that observations from the same participant may be related.
Cluster-robust covariance protects coefficient uncertainty against unspecified within-participant dependence under its large-cluster assumptions; it does not remove serial structure from residuals or change the fitted conditional mean. Participant-day repetition and within-day temporal dependence are therefore also examined directly in model checks and sensitivity analyses.

Omnibus test, category contrasts, and site-average estimates
The primary omnibus is a six-restriction Wald F test that all six non-reference light-source coefficients equal zero. The near-eye test is the preregistered primary inference; the chest test is complementary. The six non-reference ratios to indoor electric light form one multiplicity family within placement and receive a false-discovery-rate (FDR) adjustment using the Benjamini–Hochberg method. Category means and ratios are site-average estimates: each site receives equal weight on the fitted log-mean scale before one back-transformation to melEDI in lux. This is a geometric expectation, not the arithmetic mean of response-scale site predictions.

Category-by-site interaction
The association between light-source category and melEDI is allowed to differ by study site in a model examined separately from the additive primary omnibus. The near-eye frame supports the literal interaction:
geo_medi_1h ~ site * light_source
The chest frame lacks all categories at the near-eye-only Munich (DE) site and is therefore represented by one coefficient for each observed site-category cell:
geo_medi_1h ~ 0 + site_source_cell
The second expression is an equivalent saturated observed-cell parameterization, not a different scientific estimand. Its restriction matrix tests whether the observed cells can be represented additively by site plus light source. The models use the same log link, quasi-Tweedie variance, participant-clustered HC1 covariance, and geometric site-average estimation as the additive models.

Descriptive model performance
Squared-error and working-deviance summaries were calculated from the full category-by-site interaction models, so the interaction contribution is retained. These quantities describe in-sample fit and are not inferential substitutes for the omnibus tests. The participant-hour version weights every retained hour equally; the participant-balanced version first gives each participant equal total weight. The working-deviance version uses the quasi-Tweedie mean-variance relationship. Because these loss functions differ, their R-squared values are not interchangeable. The Shapley allocation averages a component’s contribution across all orders in which components could be added, allocating shared fitted-model information rather than counting it repeatedly; these are point summaries without uncertainty intervals.

All five hierarchy-valid nested fits converged without warnings, had positive-definite Hessians, and were non-singular. The model contains no random light-source slopes, participant-day effect, or AR(1) term. Residual dependence and the zero process remain imperfectly represented: the lag-one Pearson residual correlation was 0.288, while the observed and Tweedie-implied zero fractions were 0.278 and 0.398.
These point summaries are descriptive, model-dependent, non-causal, do not have uncertainty intervals, and are not a unique allocation of exposure variation. The assessment does not replace the accepted population-mean primary model or change its omnibus test or multiplicity families. It is distinct from the separate within-participant and between-participant sensitivity, which is a population-mean quasi-Tweedie augmentation with participant-clustered covariance. That sensitivity is not a mixed model, random-intercept model, random-slope model, or variance-component analysis. The corresponding reader-facing auxiliary result retains the same boundary.

Both additive models converged without warnings, were full rank, and had finite positive-definite participant-clustered covariance. Large dispersion and residual spread show that the working variance is only an approximation. Hours close together in time still show similar unexplained deviations: the technical lag-one Pearson residual correlations were 0.478 near eye and 0.615 at chest within contiguous participant-day sequences. Clustered covariance allows within-participant residual dependence when estimating uncertainty, but does not make these correlations vanish.
Zero mass and residual shape
The fixed-power Tweedie working model substantially overpredicted exact zeros: the observed overall fractions were 0.278 near eye and 0.277 at chest, compared with working expectations of 0.852 and 0.948. This is a distributional limitation, not evidence that observed zeros should be removed. The analysis therefore treats the Tweedie family as a working mean-variance model, uses robust covariance, and avoids probability claims about the zero process.

title: H03 analysis preparation and provenance
text:
5. Predefined sensitivities
One sensitivity uses the gap-timing-unaware dataset. It still passes the general requirement of at least 50% valid minutes per hour and at least 80% valid hours per day, but the timing of the remaining missing observations is not used for an additional metric-specific adjustment. At this first explanation only, the primary dataset could be interpreted as a time-sensitive primary metric dataset. Hereafter it is called simply the primary dataset.
Other predefined branches use the same participants and participant-hours available at both sensor positions; exclude hours that span diary-state or measurement-context boundaries; exclude site-category cells that fail the predefined support rule; vary the quasi-Tweedie working power to 1.30 and 1.80; and add participant-level category-proportion terms to separate within-participant from between-participant information. The same-participant, same-hour comparison uses separately fitted placement estimates and is not an equivalence test or a direct test of a sensor-position effect. These branches do not replace the primary estimand.

title: H03 analysis preparation and provenance
section: 6. Exploratory nonlinear time-of-day and linear-latitude context
text:
6. Exploratory nonlinear time-of-day and linear-latitude context
Nonlinear time-of-day GAM analysis
The nonlinear generalized additive model (GAM) analysis is exploratory and separate from the preregistered GLM inference. The association with clock time is allowed to bend across the day rather than follow a straight line. It models the raw one-hour geometric melEDI outcome with a fixed-power Tweedie mean, log link, global cyclic time smooth, sum-to-zero light-source and site deviation smooths, participant-specific smooths, and participant-day random intercepts:
geo_medi_1h ~
  s(time_hour, bs = "cc", k = 12) +
  s(time_hour, light_source, bs = "sz", k = 12) +
  s(time_hour, site, bs = "sz", k = 12) +
  s(time_hour, participant, bs = "fs", k = 10) +
  s(participant_day, bs = "re")
The sum-to-zero smooths add category- and site-specific deviations to the global cyclic time-of-day smooth; indoor electric light is not a smooth reference. bam() used fREML, discrete computation, cyclic knots at 0 and 24 hours, and a second fit with an AR(1) working error parameter estimated from the preliminary standardized residual lag-1 correlation. Participant, participant-day, and site smooths remain in the fitted model but are excluded from the displayed population curves. The stored figure curves form a site-average by giving sites equal weight and then omit unsupported time points from the display.

Linear absolute-latitude context
The exploratory ecological replacement of site uses centered absolute latitude and its category interaction:
geo_medi_1h ~ light_source * absolute_latitude_centered_10deg
It uses the same quasi-Tweedie working power and log link, but uncertainty is clustered by site because latitude varies only between sites. title: H04: Self-reported activity and measured personal light exposure
text:
Terms used below


Site-average estimate: an average across the observed sites that gives each site equal weight on the fitted log-mean scale.

Activity-by-site interaction: a model term that allows the association between activity and melEDI to differ by study site.

95% CI: a confidence interval that summarizes statistical uncertainty around an estimate.

FDR: a false-discovery-rate adjustment applied within a declared family of comparisons.

Random intercept: a term that lets participants have different overall exposure levels while retaining the fixed activity-by-site structure.

Nonlinear GAM analysis: a generalized additive model analysis in which activity- and site-associated patterns may bend across clock time.

AR(1): a first-order autoregressive structure that allows adjacent residuals to be more alike than residuals farther apart.

Shapley allocation: a descriptive allocation that distributes shared fitted-model information instead of summing overlapping contributions.

Common sample: the same participants and participant-hours observed at both sensor positions.

title: H04: Self-reported activity and measured personal light exposure
text:
Exploratory participant random-intercept decomposition
The accepted population-mean models use participant-clustered covariance and do not contain random effects. A separate descriptive mixed model was fitted to quantify how much model-based variation is associated with the fixed activity-by-site structure and with participant-level variation. The random intercept lets participants have different overall exposure levels while retaining the fixed activity-by-site structure:
geo_medi_1h ~ site * activity_named + (1 | participant)
The model used a Tweedie distribution with a log link, maximum likelihood, and the same fixed working power of 1.539919. It retained the supported five named categories, so Other-only hours were not included. Every retained participant-hour still contributed exactly one unit through its 1/k membership weights. Five hierarchy-valid models allocated marginal R² to activity, study site, and their interaction. The participant random intercept then supplied the difference between conditional and marginal R².
This model has no participant-specific activity slope and no participant-day random effect. It is separate from the population-mean Mundlak-style sensitivity, which adjusts current-category contrasts for each participant’s usual activity composition. Neither assessment changes the primary analysis or its multiplicity families.

Point estimates use Nakagawa’s lognormal distribution-specific variance convention. The fixed linear predictor uses a fractional-frequency sample variance with exact 1/k weights, so each participant-hour sums to one. No bootstrap intervals were calculated. The allocation averages the two valid entry orders for activity and site, and adds their interaction only after both main effects.








Marginal R² was 0.766 near eye and 0.768 at chest. Conditional R² was 0.858 and 0.859, respectively. The participant intercept therefore added about 0.092 at each sensor position. Activity accounted for 80.7% of near-eye and 86.1% of chest marginal R², compared with 12.5% and 5.9% for study site and 6.9% and 8.0% for the interaction. A one-SD participant intercept corresponded to a 2.02-fold near-eye and 2.05-fold chest conditional expected mean while holding activity and site fixed. This common multiplier is not a participant-specific activity slope.
All ten nested fits converged without warnings, had positive-definite Hessians, and were non-singular. Aggregated participant-hour Pearson residuals retained lag-one correlations of 0.317 near eye and 0.301 at chest. Observed exact-zero fractions were 0.294 and 0.301, compared with mixed-model Tweedie-implied fractions of 0.410 and 0.429. The decomposition is consequently an exploratory point description, not evidence of calibrated individual-hour prediction or a causal partition. The conventional unweighted expanded-row marginal R² was 0.768 and 0.770, only slightly higher than the required weighted values, but it gives multi-select hours excess influence and is not the reported estimand. These mixed-model R² values are not interchangeable with the quasi-deviance and squared-error summaries above.
Random-intercept assessment estimates, model diagnostics, hierarchy-respecting allocation, and nested-model checks provide the complete stored point estimates and checks.

title: H04: Self-reported activity and measured personal light exposure
text:
Detailed analysis record
The exact sample-flow and model-ready dataset definitions are documented in Preparation 02 and Preparation 06. The companion How the H04 analysis was prepared traces the verified inputs, multi-select transformation, model frames, estimands, model checks, sensitivities, temporal construction, and recorded output chain behind this report.
Preregistration changes


Study-site structure (DEV-013). The accepted population-average category model uses fixed study-site adjustment, while a separate activity-by-site interaction model evaluates variation among sites. The site interaction does not redefine the primary omnibus test.

Response model (DEV-014). Fixed-power quasi-Tweedie log-mean models with participant-clustered covariance replace the registered Gaussian mixed model. They describe multiplicative mean comparisons and are not treated as calibrated zero-generating distributions.

Multi-label activity representation (DEV-025). The analysis collapses the three outdoor flags before pivoting, removes duplicate labels within an hour, gives each of k concurrent retained categories weight 1/k, and retains Other only when it is the sole selected category for descriptive display.

Primary and site-interaction questions (DEV-026). The additive site-plus-activity model supplies the primary activity omnibus; the separate activity-by-site interaction model supplies descriptive category means, ratios, and site-specific variation.

Multiple-testing adjustment (DEV-027). False-discovery-rate adjustment is applied to each explicitly assembled complete activity or site-interaction contrast family.
Exact category estimates

title: H04 analysis preparation and provenance
text:
NoteAbout this analysis record



This page explains how verified one-hour melEDI records and multi-select self-reported activity reports were turned into the scientific results. The H04 results report presents the findings and its preregistration changes.


H04 asks whether hourly self-reported activity categories are associated with hourly geometric mean melanopic equivalent daylight illuminance (melEDI), a melanopsin-weighted measure of illuminance expressed in lux. The primary near-eye sensor position measures light near the eyes but is not a retinal measurement. The complementary chest sensor position is not a measure of ocular exposure. The five interpretable categories are At home, Office/home working, Outdoors, Vehicle/public transport, and Sleeping. Other/unspecified activity remains in the additive population-mean model as a display-only row, is a varied display-only category rather than a coherent scientific category, and supports no substantive claim.
Activity categories are not mutually exclusive behavioural states. When an hour contains several retained labels, that hour contributes 1/k to each of its k labels. The central category estimand is therefore average melEDI associated with each reported collapsed activity category, with the hour’s contribution shared across concurrent reports. It is not a causal effect.
A participant-hour is one original hourly record for one participant; the concurrent selections share that one hour rather than creating independent duplicates. A participant-day groups that participant’s records within one study day.
A site-average estimate is an average across the observed study sites that gives each site equal weight. The activity-by-site interaction model allows the association between activity category and melEDI to differ by study site.
This page identifies the data and code that produced the result, explains why each operation was needed, and shows the recorded evidence used to check it. Shared coverage and model-ready dataset definitions are documented in Preparation 02 and Preparation 06.

title: H05: Habitual light-related behaviour and personal light exposure
text:
Orientation
The four scores describe spending time outdoors (F2), devices in bed (F3), ambient light before bedtime (F4), and morning/daytime light use (F5). F2 includes one reverse-coded item; F3–F5 are sums of their ordered items. Every factor score was complete. Within each exact model sample, the score was centred and expressed both per raw point and per participant-level standard deviation. The report uses one participant-level SD so estimates can be compared across the four differently ranged factor scores.
Near-eye measurements are primary because they more closely represent light near the eyes. All available chest measurements are analysed separately as complementary evidence and are not interpreted as ocular exposure. A participant-day is one eligible local calendar day from one participant; daily metrics can therefore contribute repeated days from the same person. A common-sample analysis fits the near-eye and chest models to the same participants and participant-days at both sensor positions, so separately fitted placement estimates are not confused with differences in who contributed data. This is neither an equivalence test nor a direct test of a placement effect, and the placements are never pooled as independent observations.
The 95% confidence interval (CI) describes uncertainty around each reported effect. False-discovery-rate (FDR) adjustment limits the expected proportion of false discoveries across the complete planned family. The main models treat study site as a fixed effect, meaning that each study site receives its own adjustment. A random effect instead represents variation attributed to a grouping variable, such as participant or study site, rather than estimating a separate coefficient for each group. A sensitivity analysis repeats an accepted comparison under a predefined alternative to assess whether the interpretation is stable.

Model checks and the unfit sleep-environment boundary
Most near-eye and complementary chest models were acceptable or acceptable with specified limitations. The four sleep-environment cells at each placement are unfit for H05 inference because their simulated residuals and fitted response support show material failures. Their estimates, confidence intervals, and p-values are suppressed. This judgment applies only to the H05 response and model structure. It does not rule out analysing the underlying metric in another hypothesis with a different response variable, estimand, or model structure.
A Tweedie model is a positive-response regression model that can accommodate right-skewed outcomes and exact zeros. For the sleep-environment outcome, that working model did not provide a defensible inferential representation.

title: H05: Habitual light-related behaviour and personal light exposure
text:
MDER results and upper-tail checks
A predefined sensitivity uses the gap-timing-unaware dataset. It applies the same general 50%-per-hour and 80%-per-day coverage rules, but does not use the timing of remaining missing observations for metric-specific adjustment. For this contrast only, the approved primary preparation could be interpreted as a time-sensitive primary metric dataset. Below, it is called simply the primary dataset.
MDER is the arithmetic mean of viable one-minute melEDI/illuminance ratios. Both channels must be finite and strictly positive, and at least 720 of the complete 1,440 local wall-clock minutes must provide a viable ratio. Repeated local minutes on a daylight-saving fall-back day are averaged channel by channel before the ratio is formed; absent spring-forward minutes remain missing. Each viable minute ratio has equal weight, so MDER is not a ratio of daily integrals. Failure of this support rule makes only MDER missing.
The gap-timing-unaware dataset left the family-wide conclusion unchanged; its exact 478-day MDER placement comparison retained all four directions with overlapping component intervals.
No MDER association retained FDR-supported evidence. The small complementary chest coefficients were more sensitive to upper-tail observations, but their sensitivity intervals still crossed zero.

title: H05: Habitual light-related behaviour and personal light exposure
text:
Interpretation and limitations
The strongest defensible conclusion is that, after fixed-site adjustment and one complete 68-test FDR adjustment, these data provide no multiplicity-retained evidence that any of the four LEBA factors is associated with the 17 selected personal light-exposure metrics.
The positive F2 estimates for time above 1,000 lx melEDI and melEDI dose are consistent across the principal stability checks. Their confidence intervals describe non-zero associations before multiplicity adjustment, but their adjusted values do not support confirmatory claims. They should be treated as descriptive patterns that may motivate future work, not as established effects of spending time outdoors.
This is an observational association analysis. LEBA scores are self-reported, site adjustment cannot remove all person-level confounding, only nine sites contribute to the primary analysis, and several small estimates are sensitive to site omission. Near-eye and chest measurements also represent related but non-identical light fields. Finally, the sleep-environment Tweedie models are unfit for inference because of material response-support and simulated-residual failures; their estimates and p-values are suppressed from the reader-facing results and cannot support a claim in H05. This judgment is specific to the response variable and model structure used here and does not preclude analysing the metric in another hypothesis with a different response or model.
Uncertainty remains: several small estimates changed direction when a site was omitted, the small complementary chest MDER coefficients were sensitive to upper-tail observations but retained zero-crossing sensitivity intervals, and the four planned sleep-environment models are unfit for H05 inference under this response definition and model structure.

Models, response specifications, and inference
For participant-day outcomes, the full model asks whether LEBA improves the site-adjusted description while accounting for repeated days from the same participant. Its participant random effect represents remaining between-participant variation after LEBA and site are considered. The reduced model removes only LEBA. Interdaily stability (IS) and intradaily variability (IV) have one response per participant, so they do not use a participant random effect. Fixed site effects use the registered site order and sum-to-zero contrasts; the LEBA coefficient is therefore adjusted for site without being tied to one reference site. This adjustment describes site differences and does not imply that site causes an exposure outcome. The registered random-site structure is retained as a sensitivity analysis.
The following evaluated cell reads and prints the exact formula objects used for the full, reduced, and registered random-site sensitivity models.

registered_formula <- function(analysis_unit, formula_id) {
  row <- formula_registry |>
    dplyr::filter(
      .data$analysis_unit == .env$analysis_unit,
      .data$formula_id == .env$formula_id
    )
  stopifnot(nrow(row) == 1L)
  stats::as.formula(row$formula[[1L]])
}

h05_formulas <- list(
  participant_day_full = registered_formula("participant_day", "fixed_full"),
  participant_day_reduced = registered_formula("participant_day", "fixed_reduced"),
  participant_full = registered_formula("participant", "fixed_full"),
  participant_reduced = registered_formula("participant", "fixed_reduced"),
  participant_day_random_site = registered_formula("participant_day", "random_site"),
  participant_random_site = registered_formula("participant", "random_site")
)

tibble::tibble(
  Model = c(
    "Participant-day primary full",
    "Participant-day primary reduced",
    "Participant primary full",
    "Participant primary reduced",
    "Participant-day random-site sensitivity",
    "Participant random-site sensitivity"
  ),
  `Exact Wilkinson formula` = paste0(
    "`",
    vapply(h05_formulas, deparse1, character(1)),
    "`"
  )
) |>
  gt::gt(rowname_col = "Model") |>
  gt::fmt_markdown(columns = `Exact Wilkinson formula`) |>
  gt::cols_width(`Exact Wilkinson formula` ~ gt::pct(67)) |>
  gt::tab_source_note(
    source_note = paste(
      "The table is evaluated directly from the registered formula objects;",
      "the reduced model removes only LEBA from the corresponding full model."
    )
  ) |>
  h05_gt(12)

Gaps cannot be mistaken for a continuously observed period.

Current scientific deviations

Placement roles and matched comparison: DEV-001, REP-001, and REP-002.
Site-adjusted H05 association models rather than pooled correlations: DEV-028.
Four factors × 17 metrics and complete 68-test FDR families: DEV-029.
Current window, timing, and continuous-period rules: DEV-054.
Current mean of viable one-minute MDER ratios: DEV-058.

Resolved implementation history

Complete-vector FDR adjustment replaced the historical scalar adjustment: IMP-001.
Site-adjusted model inference replaced the historical inconsistent correlation display: IMP-006.

title: H05: Habitual light-related behaviour and personal light exposure
text:
Source data and technical provenance
Exact source-data links accompany each result, model-check display, and sensitivity analysis above. The full data-preparation, model-construction, model-check, and output lineage is documented in the H05 analysis preparation and provenance.

Implementation history for the current MDER and numerical-zero rules
The current MDER outputs were produced by bounded MDER-only updates that preserved all non-MDER raw tests and fitted objects. The primary and gap-timing-unaware preservation records are the MDER reconciliation and gap MDER reconciliation.
For darkest-10-hour mean melEDI, applying the current numerical-zero rule changed three primary near-eye and five primary chest participant-days from approximately 4.16 × 10-17 lx to exactly 0 lx without changing a fitted sample. Only the corresponding primary models, model checks, influence checks, matched comparison, and mathematically dependent complete FDR families were updated. Coefficients changed by at most 3.61 × 10-12 per LEBA point; two adjusted p-values changed below three-decimal display precision, no family rank changed, and all three families retained zero of 68 associations. The gap-timing-unaware L10 values were already exact zeros and were not refitted.

title: H05 analysis preparation and provenance
text:
NoteAbout this analysis record



This page explains how verified light-exposure metrics and questionnaire scores were turned into the H05 results. Rendering it recalculates only file-identity, schema, and key checks plus lightweight descriptive summaries from the stored H05 model frames. It reads fitted models, estimates, intervals, model checks, influence screens, and predefined alternative analyses from their recorded files. It does not fit or refit a model, calculate predictions, repeat model checks, rerun leave-one-site-out analyses, bootstrap, or simulate data.


H05 asks whether four Light Exposure Behaviour Assessment (LEBA) questionnaire factors are associated with 17 personal light-exposure metrics. The primary analysis uses the near-eye sensor position, which measures light close to the eyes. All-available chest measurements provide complementary evidence but are not interpreted as ocular exposure. A participant-day is one eligible local calendar day from one participant; participant-day metrics can therefore include repeated days from the same person.
Factor effects are reported per one participant-level standard deviation (SD) of the score, with a 95% confidence interval (95% CI). Each inferential placement or dataset applies false-discovery-rate (FDR) adjustment to the complete family of four factors × 17 metrics = 68 tests. Participant-level and participant-day metrics use different model structures but share the same fixed-site adjustment, which estimates one adjustment coefficient for each study site, as well as the same questionnaire-score scaling and family definition.
This page identifies the data and code that produced those results, explains why each analytical operation was necessary, and shows the stored evidence used to check the analysis. Read it alongside the H05 results report; the exact H05 linked registration-record summary is mapped there once.

title: H05 analysis preparation and provenance
text:
3. Models, estimands, and inference
Estimand, practical effects, uncertainty, and multiplicity
For each metric and factor, the full model adds the centred LEBA score to the reduced site-adjusted model. A likelihood-ratio comparison asks whether the full model describes the data better than the reduced model on a common likelihood basis. The raw inferential p-value comes from that comparison. Each declared family contains all 17 metrics × 4 factors = 68 tests, and FDR adjustment is performed on the complete 68-value vector. Support is retained at adjusted p ≤ 0.050, decided before display formatting.
Back-transformation converts a fitted-scale coefficient into the practical response scale used for interpretation. Coefficients are back-transformed and reported per one participant-level LEBA SD. Gaussian identity outcomes return a difference in the stated metric unit, log-transformed and Tweedie outcomes return a ratio, IS returns an odds ratio, and clock-time outcomes return a difference in hours. Every reported 95% CI is a two-sided Wald interval from the final model. No secondary significance screen is attached to descriptive sensitivities.

  `H05-F2-complementary-chest` = "Complementary chest",

)

NoteWhy a less conservative adjustment can accompany fewer retained associations



For one unchanged vector of raw p-values, the complete-vector FDR adjustment used here cannot retain fewer associations than Bonferroni at the same 0.050 threshold. The H05 family above is based on likelihood-ratio p-values from the fixed-site models. It is therefore not interchangeable with a family built from unadjusted rank correlations or another raw test. Multiplicity adjustment and the construction of the raw p-values are separate analytical decisions; the latter can change which associations enter the smallest ranks before either correction is applied.


Site specification
A fixed site effect gives each study site its own adjustment coefficient. A random site effect instead represents between-site variation through one estimated variance component. The fixed-site primary specification differs from the registered random-site structure. The decision was based on the inherited 17-metric site-structure evidence: every fixed-site model converged with a positive-definite Hessian and none was singular, whereas the random-site descriptions contained unstable, non-estimable, and singular fits. Keeping site fixed also estimates each site’s adjustment directly rather than relying on a variance component from only nine sites. This is an adjustment for observed site differences, not a claim that site causes an exposure outcome. The random-site structure remains a sensitivity.

4. Model checks and influence
Model-check sequence
Every stored final model was checked for convergence, Hessian status, singularity, residual behaviour, response bounds, metric-specific timing support, and within-participant serial dependence where applicable. Gaussian models use transformed-residual and influence checks. Tweedie models add simulation-based uniformity, dispersion, zero-support, and outlier checks. Candidate influential participants were ranked by Cook’s distance for ordinary linear models or by maximum absolute Pearson residual for mixed models; this screen did not silently remove observations.
The compact table below excludes the sleep-environment metric because that outcome has a separate, stronger disposition immediately afterwards.

NoteSleep-environment outcome: unfit for H05 inference



The four primary near-eye models for time below 1 lx melEDI during sleep are unfit for H05 inference. The observed response contains exact zeros, while the fitted Tweedie simulations generated none; simulation-based uniformity and outlier checks also showed material failure, and fitted values crossed the admissible response support. Their coefficients, intervals, and p-values are therefore suppressed from the H05 results. The complementary chest models show the same material response-support and simulated-residual limitations and are also not used as inferential evidence.
This disposition is specific to this outcome as the H05 response under this model structure. It does not mean that the sleep-environment metric cannot be analysed in another hypothesis that uses a different response variable, estimand, or model structure.

6. Current numerical-zero and MDER qualifications
Numerical-zero normalization for darkest-10-hour mean melEDI
The current rule sets a geometric-mean back-transformation residual to exact zero only when it lies within the unit-aware floating-point tolerance and every finite source minute entering the selected window is exactly zero. For these L10 windows, the tolerance is 2.220446049250313 × 10-14 lx. Missing source minutes remain missing and are never imputed as zero.
Under this rule, three primary near-eye and five primary chest participant-days are exact zero rather than approximately 4.163336342344337 × 10-17 lx. This does not change a fitted sample, any non-L10 value, hourly or 30-minute value, participant-level value, or site/daylight-context value. The gap-timing-unaware L10 values were already exact zeros.
MDER samples and upper-tail influence
The accepted MDER input is the daily arithmetic mean of viable one-minute melEDI/illuminance ratios described above. Its exact all-available samples, upper-tail screen, and bounded influence refits are summarized below. Changes are expressed relative to the full-model standard error (SE). The outer-fence rule identifies observations for sensitivity checks; it is not an exclusion rule.

The current sample contains 702 near-eye participant-days from 137 participants at nine sites and 732 chest participant-days from 152 participants at eight sites. One near-eye and three chest days exceeded the outer fence. All 44 day- and participant-deletion refits passed, and every chest sensitivity interval contained zero. The four near-eye F5 sensitivity intervals remained below zero, consistent with its unadjusted primary interval, but that association is not retained after complete-family FDR adjustment. The small chest coefficients were more upper-tail-sensitive than the near-eye coefficients, including one sign reversal for a coefficient already close to zero. No observation was removed from the primary analysis.
The gap-timing-unaware samples contain 687 near-eye participant-days from 137 participants and 723 chest participant-days from 152 participants. The paired/common comparison contains 478 days from 107 participants at eight sites, with all four directions concordant and all component intervals overlapping. One near-eye and three chest days exceeded the outer fence. All 44 gap deletion refits passed and 40 intervals contained zero. The near-eye coefficients changed by at most 0.233 full-model standard errors without a sign reversal; the small chest F2 coefficient reversed direction in two deletions, and every chest interval contained zero. The gap-timing-unaware near-eye family retained zero of 68 associations after FDR adjustment.
The upper-tail summary and influence-refit record retain the exact primary inputs, samples, and influence results. The gap-timing-unaware analysis has a separate influence record and paired/common comparison.

The bounded updater replaced eight primary inferential L10 bundles, rebuilt eight registered random-site sensitivities and 36 primary L10 leave-one-site-out refits, and refreshed the matched primary placement comparison. It ran zero gap-timing-unaware L10 and zero non-L10 refits. All 22 frozen-scope reconciliation checks pass; the exact result-change, complete-family, input-cell, and preservation records are linked through the L10 artifact-update manifest.
The bounded MDER updates likewise preserved all non-MDER raw tests and fitted objects. The primary MDER reconciliation contains 20 preservation checks. The gap MDER reconciliation contains 16 checks and records 27 non-MDER FDR-adjusted p-value changes and 26 rank changes caused solely by replacing the four MDER slots in the gap-timing-unaware family; every non-MDER raw test and fitted object is unchanged.

The H05 preparation-report manifest is created after the final website render. It records complete identities for the authoring source, the byte-identical website QMD copy, rendered HTML, page assets, H05 scripts and tests, scientific outputs, source data, shared configuration snapshot, and R environment. The manifest excludes itself and the handoff that quotes its identity, preventing a circular checksum chain.
How to examine or reproduce H05
A reader can follow the analysis in five passes:

inspect H05_input_audit.csv, h05_contract.R, and the factor, metric, formula, and run registries to verify the frozen inputs and specifications;
compare the exact samples above with H05_model_frame_index.csv and the 136 frames in H05_model_frames.rds;
follow run_h05_stage2.R through h05_modeling.R, then the bounded MDER and L10 reseal scripts, to connect each frame to its current model object, coefficient, interval, likelihood-ratio test, diagnostic, and sensitivity record;
inspect the complete 68-value family audit before interpreting any individual association; and
read the H05 results report alongside its tables, figures, and paired source data.

The most important boundary is that the preparation record documents a frozen analysis; it does not create an alternate result. If an input, metric rule, response model, or estimand changes, the affected scientific pipeline must be rerun before this page is refreshed.

title: H06: Day type, exercise, sleep, and personal light exposure
text:
The preregistered hypothesis was:

H6: Day type, daily exercise, and sleep variables predict daily light exposure metrics.

The main H06 analysis deliberately narrows that broad question to the zero-aware geometric mean of melanopic equivalent daylight illuminance (melEDI) in each observed one-hour interval that met the support criteria. It asks whether estimated mean hourly near-eye melEDI differs for free versus work days, active versus sedentary day status, and per one additional hour of previous sleep. It averages over retained hours rather than estimating daily light-exposure metrics. Time of day is examined separately and exploratorily. Near-eye measurements are primary; chest measurements provide complementary, non-ocular evidence. Neither position is a direct retinal measure.
The complementary participant-day analysis, which treats one calendar day from one participant as the analytical unit, addresses daily light-exposure metrics. It is complementary evidence, while this hourly report remains the main H06 analysis. The two reports answer related but different questions, so their estimates are not interchangeable.
How the hourly H06 analysis was prepared traces the inputs, fitted samples, formulas, model checks, sensitivity analyses, and source data underlying this report.






NoteAnswer in brief




Primary result. After false-discovery-rate adjustment, activity status (FDR-adjusted p < 0.001) and day type (FDR-adjusted p = 0.004) met the adjusted 0.050 threshold. Previous sleep did not (FDR-adjusted p = 0.745).
Qualification. The day-type association is site- and model-dependent. Chest, paired-day, dataset-sensitivity, and model-check results provide complementary qualifications. The primary conclusions were also stable in a near-eye-only sensitivity that excluded six participants outside the employment requirement.
Timing context. The nonlinear clock-time analysis is exploratory. Its intervals describe individual displayed times, not a simultaneous or multiplicity-controlled whole-curve test.

All reported associations are observational.

title: H06: Day type, exercise, sleep, and personal light exposure
text:
Reader orientation
A participant-hour is one observed one-hour interval from one participant that met the support criteria; a participant-day is one calendar day contributed by one participant. The analysis reports the estimated mean hourly melEDI among observed hours that met the support criteria. Because participant-days contribute different numbers of retained participant-hours, the main estimand gives more weight to days with more observed hours.
Near-eye measurements are primary because the sensor position is closer to ocular light exposure. Chest measurements are complementary, non-ocular evidence. Neither sensor is a direct retinal measure.
A participant-cluster-robust 95% confidence interval (95% CI) allows observations from the same participant to be related and uses the HC3 small-sample correction. False-discovery-rate adjustment is used for each declared set of related tests and is abbreviated FDR below. A predictor-by-site interaction model allows an association to differ by study site. Its site-average estimate is an average across sites that gives each site equal weight. A sensitivity analysis asks whether a conclusion changes when a defined feature of the dataset, sample, covariance correction, working variance, site weighting, calendar label, participant or site inclusion, or response model is changed.
